pairings.reason: Both arms share the same upstream fault — scene_ids lists sc-024 and locations lists DARK STREET, neither of which the scene layer records — which depresses Referential integrity (B) to 3 for both equally and is not forgiven. Arm-A additionally carries a load-bearing internal contradiction: Neo's status and safety entry-states place him 'in the Agents' custody, handcuffed' at the event's start, which the node's own action and the grounding deny (he is alone in his apartment), and arm-A's summary presents the implanted creature as present reality, an unflagged leakage from outside the text (R2=3). Arm-B fixes both: it frames the body-horror as 'a nightmare he has woken from' (R2=4) and keeps Neo's entry-states consistent with the grounding. Arm-B also obeys the register contract more cleanly, giving objects only physical/positional/status while moving the phone, car door, and bridge on status, and it records more genuine changes (V1/V3 slightly stronger). Neither arm reaches the gate (mean ≥ 4.0; both sit near 3.1), so both would quarantine, but a rational producer ships arm-B as the better basis for revision because it is internally consistent and leakage-resistant where arm-A is not.
